s1.syndrome_frame: bilateral breast lumps with suspicious masses and lymphadenopathy
salient_findings: left breast lump fixed to the chest wall
irregular spiculated mass in the left breast on MRI
key_facts: 48-year-old woman
type 2 diabetes
hypertension
bilateral breast lumps of one-week duration
no family history of breast or ovarian cancer
regular menstrual cycles
left breast lump 4 × 4 cm hard and fixed to the chest wall
right breast lump 1 × 1 cm firm and mobile
MRI showed irregular spiculated mass in the left breast
MRI showed well-defined lesion in the right breast
bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy on MRI
ultrasound and bone scan negative for metastases
fine-needle aspiration cytology of the left breast lump showed malignant cells
FNAC of the left axillary lymph node showed malignant cells
core-needle biopsy of the left breast confirmed infiltrative duct cell carcinoma
estrogen- and progesterone-receptor positive

salient_findings: left breast lump fixed to the chest wall
irregular spiculated mass in the left breast on MRI

no family history of breast or ovarian cancer

bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy on MRI

shortlist.label: invasive ductal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: confirmed by core-needle biopsy of the left breast

shortlist.label: inflammatory breast cancer
shortlist.why_kept: bilateral breast lumps and lymphadenopathy, although no classic signs of inflammation

shortlist.label: lobular carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: bilateral involvement, but less likely given the distinct characteristics of each lump

shortlist.label: phyllodes tumor
shortlist.why_kept: rapid growth and large size of the left breast lump, although biopsy results do not support this diagnosis

shortlist.label: metastatic cancer
shortlist.why_kept: bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy, but primary cancer is already identified as invasive ductal carcinoma

raw.rationale: The presence of a hard, fixed lump in the left breast, MRI findings of an irregular spiculated mass, and fine-needle aspiration cytology showing poorly cohesive clusters of ductal cells with pleomorphism, hyperchromasia, and prominent nucleoli, along with core-needle biopsy confirmation of infiltrative duct cell carcinoma, strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: inflammatory breast cancer
rejected.why: There is no mention of characteristic symptoms such as diffuse erythema, edema, or warmth of the breast skin, which are typical for inflammatory breast cancer.

rejected.label: lobular carcinoma
rejected.why: The cytology and biopsy results specifically mention ductal cells, not lobular cells, which are characteristic of lobular carcinoma.

rejected.label: phyllodes tumor
rejected.why: The description of the left breast lump and cytology results does not match the typical features of a phyllodes tumor, which often presents as a large, rapidly growing mass with a mix of stromal and epithelial components.

rejected.label: metastatic cancer
rejected.why: There is no evidence of a primary cancer elsewhere in the body, and the ultrasound and bone scan were negative for metastases, making metastatic cancer to the breast less likely.
